claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about the child or children you want to claim Child Benefit for.

**How old is the child (or what are the ages of the children) you're claiming for?**

Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age, so I need to know:
- Are they under 16?
- Between 16-19 years old?
- 20 years or older?

Please tell me the age(s) of the child/children, and I can guide you through the eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 15 years old, that means they fall into the "under 16" category. Children under 16 automatically qualify as long as certain other conditions are met.

Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check on Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

This is an important eligibility requirement. Children in full-time work (24+ hours per week) may not qualify unless they're also in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just focused on school at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex doesn't work at all, that satisfies that requirement. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

These are benefits that would make them ineligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're only 15, so they don't claim anything themselves.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits, let me move to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

The rules vary by country:
- **In England**: All types of apprenticeships would disqualify them
- **In Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify them
- **In Wales**: Most apprenticeships disqualify them, EXCEPT Foundation Apprenticeships which are approved
- If Alex is NOT in an apprenticeship at all, that's fine too

Since Alex is 15 and focused on school, I'm assuming they're not in an apprenticeship, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex hasn't started any apprenticeship. They're still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since Alex is still in school and not in any apprenticeship, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that could make you eligible. Let me ask:

**Where do you normally live?**

The main options are:
1. **Normally live in the UK** - If you normally live in the UK, you meet the requirement
2. **EU Settlement Scheme** - If you have settled or pre-settled status, there are different pathways depending on your circumstances (working, studying, seeking work, etc.)
3. **Crown servant abroad** - If you're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Can you tell me: Do you normally live in the UK, or is your situation related to EU Settlement Scheme status or Crown service?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK, that satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. There are several ways you can qualify:

**Which of the following applies to you:**

1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex
2. **Contributing to their upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (or more) towards their care, which could include food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents
3. **Maintenance payments** - You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

You mentioned Alex lives at home with you, so I'm assuming the first option applies - you live together. Can you confirm that you live with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since you live with Alex, that confirms you're responsible for them. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- The other parent
- A grandparent or other family member
- Anyone else

Or is it just you making this claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you're the only person claiming for Alex, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is currently living:

**Is Alex:**
- In hospital?
- In care (residential or group care)?
- Fostered by you?
- Living at home normally?

Based on what you've told me, I believe Alex is living at home normally, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I'm fostering Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that! Since you're fostering Alex, let me navigate to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is an important question for fostered children:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Are you paying for Alex's accommodation and upkeep yourself (or with payments from sources other than the council)?
- Or is the local council providing payments to cover Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't get anything from the council to foster Alex - I'm covering everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you're covering all of Alex's costs yourself and the council isn't providing any payments, let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I've now worked through all the eligibility checks. Let me confirm the final step and provide you with the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

Congratulations! You meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**About Alex:**
- ✅ Age 15 (under 16 - qualifying age)
- ✅ Not working full-time (focused on school)
- ✅ Not receiving disqualifying benefits
- ✅ Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**About You:**
- ✅ Normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ Responsible for Alex as their foster carer
- ✅ You and Alex live together
- ✅ You are covering all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance costs (no council support)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of:**
   - Your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's identity and birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Evidence of your fostering arrangement

3. **Payment details:**
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks directly to your bank account
   - The current Child Benefit rate is approximately £21.15 per week for your first child

4. **Important note:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be liable for the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which could reduce or eliminate your benefit.

### For More Information:
- Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
- You can also contact HMRC if you have any questions

Best of luck with your claim! 😊
